name: Ada
title: Ada (2022 / 2012)

presenceList.meta: Ec3, Ec8, V4, V7, L1, L2, S1

type.text: **Static typing rejects mismatched use at compile time**: Every object, parameter, and function result carries a declared type, so an incompatible assignment or call is a compile error, not a run-time surprise
**Subtypes and range constraints narrow the value set**: A `subtype` refines a base type with a range or index constraint, and a value outside it raises `Constraint_Error` at the boundary
**Variant records declare a sum type**: A `case` part in a record declaration selects on a discriminant, so the alternatives are a closed, compiler-checked set
**Generic units decouple an algorithm from the types it operates on**: A `generic` declaration names formal types and subprograms, and an instantiation binds them without editing the generic body
**Access values are checked**: Dereferencing a null access value raises `Constraint_Error`, no pointer arithmetic is possible, and `access` designates a typed object
**Operator overloading makes a symbol mean whatever its package declares**: Defining `"+"` or `"="` for a private type is legal, so a reader must resolve an operator from the package that declares it

construction.text: **Package specification and body are separate units**: `package X is ... end X;` declares the visible interface and `package body X` holds the implementation, so a client compiles against the declaration
**Private types hide the representation**: `private` and `limited private` make the record fields invisible outside the package, so callers cannot couple to the layout
**Child units extend a parent without reopening it**: `package X.Y` adds declarations in its own unit, so a subsystem grows without an edit to the parent body
**Constructors are ordinary functions**: `function Make (...) return T` creates a value with no allocation and no special constructor syntax, so creation does not couple to a memory strategy
**Variables are mutable unless declared `constant`**: There is no immutability by default, so a package body holds state that clients can reach and every call must re-establish
**Library-level variables share one elaboration order**: A variable declared in a package body is initialised once, so a client's behaviour depends on when that elaboration runs
**One value, many names**: access types designate shared objects, and the parameter mode names copy semantics, not an alias set — the named flow contract is SPARK's, not Ada's

memory.text: **No garbage collector in the standard**: The storage of a declared object is reclaimed at scope exit, so reclamation timing is not coupled to a collector's pauses
**Controlled types give deterministic finalisation**: A type derived from `Ada.Finalization.Controlled` runs `Initialize`, `Adjust`, and `Finalize` at defined points, giving RAII-style cleanup
**Storage pools decouple allocation from the type**: `Storage_Pool` and `Storage_Size` are set per access type, so the allocator changes without a change to any client
**Representation clauses fix layout where needed**: `Size`, `Alignment`, and `Bit_Order` state the representation explicitly, so memory layout is declared rather than inferred
**`Unchecked_Deallocation` is manual**: An object created with `new` on the standard heap is released only by an explicit call to `Ada.Unchecked_Deallocation`, so lifetime is the programmer's duty
**There is no ownership model**: An access value can outlive its designated object after a deallocation, and the compiler does not prevent it
**Reinterpretation is a named artifact**: each `Unchecked_Conversion` is an explicit instantiation over one type pair, reviewable and provable in SPARK

error.text: **Exceptions are named and scoped**: An `exception` section handles by exception identity with `when E : Some_Error =>`, so recovery does not depend on an error code
**Language-defined checks raise exceptions instead of corrupting memory**: Range, index, discriminant, and access checks raise `Constraint_Error` or `Program_Error` at the point of violation
**Contracts raise `Assertion_Error` at the boundary**: The Ada 2012 aspects `Pre` and `Post` and type invariants check a subprogram against its callers
**An exception carries diagnostic strings**: `Ada.Exceptions.Exception_Message` and `Exception_Information` attach a message and a state snapshot to an occurrence
**No composable result type**: A fallible operation reports through `raise`, so a caller cannot thread a success-or-failure value through an ordinary expression
**`pragma Suppress` removes checks**: Suppressing a check removes the exception with it, trading safety for speed
**The runtime publishes the isolation unit**: an unraised exception terminates the task that raised it (RM 11.1, documented), and the partition survives the task

concurrency.text: **Tasking is part of the language**: `task`, `task type`, protected objects, and entries give concurrency without an external library
**Rendezvous decouples communication from shared memory**: A caller and a task meet at an `entry` and exchange parameters directly, so the task's data need not be globally visible
**Protected objects serialise access without hand-written locks**: A `protected` body runs one action at a time, so the program does not write mutex code
**`select` states waiting and timeouts declaratively**: `select ... or accept`, `or delay`, and `else` express the waiting alternatives in the construct

**Annex D states the real-time policy in code**: `pragma Priority`, `pragma Task_Dispatching_Policy (FIFO_Within_Priorities)`, and `pragma Locking_Policy (Ceiling_Locking)` declare priorities and locking
**Tasking couples a program to a run-time library**: The GNAT run time and the chosen profile decide which tasking constructs exist

platform.text: **The language is an international standard**: ISO/IEC 8652 defines the language and ISO/IEC 18009 defines conformity, so no single vendor owns it
**Several independent compilers exist**: GNAT (FSF and AdaCore) and other implementations compile the same standard
**Restricted profiles target bare hardware**: `pragma Profile (Ravenscar)` and `No_Tasking` remove constructs a small target cannot support
**Hardware access is a language feature**: `pragma Import`, `pragma Export`, and representation clauses reach registers and foreign code directly

**Certified toolchains are few**: DO-178C qualification kits and ARINC 653 bindings come from a small set of vendors, among them AdaCore, DDC-I (SCORE-Ada on Deos), and Green Hills (AdaMULTI), so a certified build couples to one of them
**Outside the certified targets, porting is unusual**: An untested platform gets few guarantees, because few ports are exercised
**The fit outside its niche is poor**: Web, data-science, and scripting work have little Ada support

performance.text: **Ahead-of-time native compilation**: GNAT emits machine code, so no interpreter and no JIT warm-up sits on the critical path
**No garbage collector**: Reclamation is deterministic, so no collector pause enters a control loop
**Inlining and representation clauses give explicit control**: `pragma Inline`, `Size`, and `Address` let a program fix code and layout where latency demands it
**The real-time policy is declared in code**: Priority and locking pragmas state the scheduling behaviour the program assumes
**Checks cost run time unless suppressed**: Range, index, and access checks are cheap but not free, and `pragma Suppress` trades them away
**The GNAT run time is large for small targets**: A tasking-enabled build needs the run time, so bare-metal work uses the restricted profiles

ecosystem.text: **The ecosystem is small and niche**: Alire and the available library set are a fraction of what mainstream languages offer
**GNAT is mature and production-quality**: The same front end serves FSF GNAT and AdaCore's GNAT Pro, and certified projects depend on it
**Alire provides a package manager**: `alr` resolves dependencies and pins toolchains, so a project build is reproducible
**Reference material is complete and stable**: The Ada Reference Manual (ISO/IEC 8652:2023), the Rationale, and the SPARK documentation are authoritative and long-lived
**The community is small**: A developer usually meets Ada through an employer's code base rather than through a public library ecosystem
**No object-code promise across compiler releases**: GNAT records the dependence graph in the .ali file, and the link step binds that pair to the same compiler release [@gnatUgn]

evolution.text: **The standard moves slowly**: Ada 2022 followed Ada 2012 by about a decade, so a needed feature waits for a revision
**Backward compatibility is strong**: Ada 2012 and Ada 2022 add features and keep earlier conforming code compiling
**GNAT tracks the current standard**: The compiler implements the latest revision and the certification profiles
**A new feature reaches users through GNAT**: Adoption follows the compiler release cycle rather than the standard's publication
**Build variants multiply**: GNAT ships the documented -pp C-style preprocessor, and guarded units select which declarations compile

domain.text: **Excellent fit for safety-critical and real-time systems**: Avionics, defense, rail, and space projects use Ada with DO-178C evidence
**Annex D and the Ravenscar profile cover hard real-time work**: Priorities, ceiling locking, and static scheduling are language-level concerns
**Representation clauses reach embedded hardware**: Registers and device layouts are declared, not accessed through undefined behaviour
**Certification artifacts are domain-specific**: A DO-178C evidence set is not reusable in another regulated domain without rework

learning.text: **The language is steep**: Tasking, generics, representation clauses, contracts, and the Annexes present several distinct models
**The surface is large**: The standard library, the Annexes, and the profiles add to the core language
**Reference material is comprehensive**: The Reference Manual states every construct, and the SPARK documentation covers the proof subset
**A regular syntax helps after the first step**: Statements end in `;` and blocks are delimited by keywords, so there is no precedence puzzle
**Tasking is the hardest single topic**: The rendezvous model and protected objects take practice to use well
**Mentors are scarce**: The small community gives fewer examples and reviews than mainstream languages offer

syntax.text: **Verbose**: `begin`/`end` pairs, full keywords, and repeated identifiers make even small programs long
**English-like and consistent**: `Ada.Text_IO.Put_Line ("x")` reads as prose, and keywords are reserved words
**Block structure is explicit**: Every construct closes with a keyword, so a reader never counts indentation
**Identifiers are `Mixed_Case` with underscores**: The convention differs from `camelCase` and `snake_case` neighbours, though it is uniform
**Qualified names add verbosity**: A fully qualified call such as `Ada.Text_IO.New_Line` is long where `use` clauses are avoided

testing.text: **Contracts are executable**: `pragma Assert`, the `Pre` and `Post` aspects, and `pragma Assertion_Policy` check invariants in the built program
**GNAT ships a test-generation tool**: `gnattest` generates AUnit test skeletons from a package specification
**GNATprove proves the stated contracts on the SPARK subset**: Sequential and concurrent SPARK code can be proved free of run-time errors
**GNATcoverage measures coverage**: The tool reports statement and branch coverage for certification evidence
**No test framework is in the language**: AUnit and `gnattest` are tools, so a suite couples to the GNAT toolchain

security.text: **Typing and checks prevent memory misuse**: Array, range, discriminant, and access checks catch violations before they become memory errors
**The standard defines the effect of constructs**: Within the defined subsets there is no undefined behaviour, and SPARK removes the remaining cases
**No pointer arithmetic**: An access value designates a typed object, so an address cannot be incremented into another object
**SPARK proves absence of run-time errors**: The subset supports proof of freedom from run-time errors and of the stated contracts
**`Unchecked_Conversion` and `System.Address` re-open the unsafe surface**: These features can defeat the type system where a program uses them

tradeoffs: **Verbosity is a deliberate trade**: `begin`/`end` pairs and spelled-out names make each construct readable at the cost of keystrokes; that is a style choice, not a dependency forced on a caller
**Restricted profiles are a scope decision**: `pragma Profile (Ravenscar)` removes dynamic task creation to make a program analysable, trading flexibility for a schedulability bound
**No garbage collector is a scope decision**: The standard leaves reclamation to the program, which suits real-time work and gives up the convenience of a collector
**Ada is not a scripting language**: Compilation and the Alire package manager assume a build step, which is a scope boundary rather than a defect
**Certification effort is a process cost**: DO-178C evidence follows from the domain's safety obligation, not from a property of the language
verdict: Ada's own constructs impose little coupling: strong static typing, package specification and body separation, generic units, tasking with protected objects, and Ada 2012 contracts each separate a caller from the thing it depends on. The cost sits in the platform and ecosystem dimension, where the language is verbose, the standard moves slowly, the library base is small, and tasking plus the Annexes take a long time to learn. For safety-critical and real-time work Ada is close to ideal; outside that niche the small ecosystem is the dominant cost.

energy.text: Compiles to native code: the fastest class in the language energy and time benchmarks [@pereira2017energy; @pereira2021ranking]. A causal re-analysis attributes the difference to execution time [@vankempen2025green].

ai-readiness.text: Sparse training data: models write it unreliably [@joel2025lowresource].

safety.text: A standards-qualified toolchain or an established safety standard covers this language.

use:verification.observation: GNATprove proves the stated contracts on the SPARK subset

delivery.note: Source compiles in the GNAT release the site installs
GNAT records the with-clause dependence graph in the .ali file, and the link step binds that pair to the same compiler release
